So ρ_S(a) = ρ(b), ρ_S(b) = ρ(a) at the two visits a,b of each selected crossing and ρ_S = ρ at vertices and unselected visits — exactly eq. carrierpr:successors and the following sentence (sm-3 101-106). ρ = `markSuccessor` is Cycle.next on `markList` = Finset.univ.sort under the order lifted from markKey = traversalKey (markPosition a) = i.val + t (CarrierMarks 79-103, Traversal 17), i.e. the def:gauss cyclic order cut at label 0; marks are ZMod n ⊕ Visit P with vertices at (i,0) and visits at (v.2, t_v) (CarrierMarks 33-40), matching "mark the traversal circle at every original vertex and every crossing visit" (sm-3 97-98). `carriers` (46-47): owner a = owner b ↔ SameCycle ρ_S a b, with `Component` the quotient by SameCycle (CarrierSmoothing 124-132) — the carriers are the cycles of ρ_S, as the adopted finite successor model (sm-3 109-112) prescribes. Faithful.

(2) "the subpolygons (or carriers) of S are the closed polygonal curves in ℝ² traced by these cycles" (excerpt 5-6). Lean: `traced_curve` (49-52) is definitional (componentPlaneCycle := map of the plane points of componentMarkList, CarrierClosedTrace 66-69). The substance is the second-round additions: `traced_marks` (102-105) — componentMarkList (= markList filtered by owner = q, CarrierClosedTrace 59-61) is Nodup, nonempty, coerces to componentCycle, and contains exactly the marks owned by q; `traced_successor` (106-109) — ρ_S(L[i]) = L[(i+1) % len], cyclically, so the inherited order IS the ρ_S-cycle order (this ties the traced list to the reconnected cycle, the round-one gap); `traced_sides` (112-120) — componentTraceEdge q i = smoothingSegment (L[i]) (the straight segment from a mark to its ρ_S-successor, CarrierAffineSegments 69-73), of positive euclideanLength (= ‖planeComplex ·‖, positive definite), end of side i = start of side i+1 (mod len), continuous. Every side is the incoming segment of its endpoint mark, and the incoming segment at each of the three mark types is certified to lie on an original edge (vertex_corner 62-64: E_{i-1}; smoothing_corner 83-85: E_{v.2}; unselected_visit_straight 125-127: E_{v.2}), so the traced curve is a closed union of straight subsegments of edges of P joined at the marks — the printed object. Faithful; see weaker_than_source for the representation note (a cyclic point list plus per-side maps rather than one set/map).

(3) "Each subpolygon Q is a closed polygon whose corners are the vertices of P it passes through and the crossing points of S it turns at (its smoothing corners)" (excerpt 6-9). Lean: `corners` (54-56) with componentCornerCycle := componentCycle.filter IsTrueCorner (CarrierTrueCorners 84-86), `IsTrueCorner S (inl _) = True`, `IsTrueCorner S (inr v) ↔ v.1 ∈ S` (CarrierTrueCorners 44-46; stmt 57-58). By mem_componentCornerCycle a corner of q is a mark owned by q that is a vertex or a selected visit. "Passes through a vertex" = owns the vertex mark, justified geometrically by vertex_corner (60-76: incoming segment ends at P i along ℓ_{i-1}, outgoing starts at P i along ℓ_i). "Exactly": `unselected_visit_straight` (124-135) certifies that at an unselected visit the incoming displacement is c₁•ℓ_{v.2} and the outgoing is c₂•ℓ_{v.2}, c₁,c₂ > 0, so the carrier passes straight through and the visit point is not a corner (dropping it does not change the curve); `smoothing_corner` (79-99) + `smoothing_corner_transverse` (137-138, det(ℓ_{v.2}, ℓ_{twin.2}) ≠ 0) certify that at a selected visit the incoming direction c₁•ℓ_i and outgoing direction c₂•ℓ_j are non-parallel, i.e. the carrier genuinely turns there — "turns at" is now rendered. Every selected crossing point that Q passes through is reached via an owned visit (sides have no marks in their interior, markSuccessor_no_mark_between), and Q turns at each, so "crossing points of S it turns at" = owned selected visits, as the Lean says. Vertices are corners by fiat in both source and Lean (no turning required at a vertex in either). Faithful.

(4) "at a smoothing corner between E_i and E_j it arrives along one of ℓ_i, ℓ_j and leaves along the other" (excerpt 9-10). Lean: `smoothing_corner` (79-99): for v.1 ∈ S owned by q, v.1.val = {v.2.val, (visitTwin v).2.val} with the two edges distinct (l. 81, so E_i, E_j are the edges of the crossing), ρ_S⁻¹(v) owned by q, incoming segment ⊆ E_{v.2} with displacement c•ℓ_{v.2}, c > 0 (82-90); ρ_S(v) = ρ(visitTwin v), owned by q, outgoing segment ⊆ E_{twin.2} with displacement c•ℓ_{twin.2}, c > 0 (91-99). This is the printed sentence made precise (it states which of ℓ_i, ℓ_j is the incoming one). Faithful, stronger.

(5) "The crossings of Q are the crossings x ∈ X(P)∖S both of whose visits lie on Q; their number is m_Q" (excerpt 10-12). Lean: `crossings_of` (140-142): x ∈ carrierCrossings q ↔ x ∉ S ∧ ∀ v, v.1 = x → owner (inr v) = q (definition CarrierCrossings 56-59; a visit "lies on Q" iff its owner is Q, which for unselected visits is the geometric fact by unselected_visit_straight). `crossing_count` (143-144): carrierCrossingCount = card (CarrierCrossings 62-64). Faithful.

(6) "A crossing in N(S) has its two visits on different subpolygons and is a crossing of no subpolygon" (excerpt 12-13). Lean: `neighbor_visits` (147-148) and `neighbor_no_carrier` (149-150) over supportNeighbors = {y | ∃ x ∈ S, Interlaces y x} (InterlaceSupports 49-52) = N(S) of def:interlace (sm-1 265-266), visits v and visitTwin v being the two visits (CarrierVisitTwin 34-62). Faithful.

(7) Domain. `SmoothingDefinitionData` (157-159) quantifies over every k with 3 ≤ k, every Generic P, every S with IsDecomposition (= S ∈ independentSupports = Ind(G_P), DecompositionDefinition 15-17; InterlaceSupports 27-42) — the section-wide "P generic" (sm-3 3-4) and "S ∈ Ind(G_P)" (excerpt 2). Nothing is vacuous: the fields are properties of concrete definitions, S = ∅ is always a decomposition, and the substantive fields (traced_successor, traced_sides, unselected_visit_straight, smoothing_corner_transverse, neighbor_visits) are genuine assertions.

Second-round summary: the three round-one gaps are closed — traced_successor ties the traced list to the ρ_S-cycle, unselected_visit_straight certifies straight passage so the corners are exactly the printed ones, and smoothing_corner_transverse renders "turns at". No printed sub-clause is without a Lean counterpart. The remaining observations (below) are representation choices or unprinted extra content, not missing or contradicted clauses.
discrepancies: Minor, non-blocking: the docstring of `unselected_visit_straight` (stmt 121-123) says the incoming AND outgoing pieces lie on the visited edge E_{v.2}, but the clause states edgeSegment membership only for the incoming piece (125-127); the outgoing piece gets only its direction (133-135: displacement = c•ℓ_{v.2}, c > 0). The printed content (no corner at an unselected visit) is fully certified by the two direction conjuncts, and the outgoing side's edge membership follows from the incoming clause of its endpoint mark, so this is a docstring overstatement rather than a fidelity gap.
stronger_than_source: `vertex_corner` (stmt 59-76): the printed definition says nothing about directions at original vertices; the Lean adds that the carrier arrives along a positive multiple of ℓ_{i-1} on E_{i-1} and leaves along a positive multiple of ℓ_i on E_i (true, unprinted).

`smoothing_corner` (79-99) is more specific than 'arrives along one of ℓ_i, ℓ_j and leaves along the other': it fixes that the carrier arrives along the edge of the visit it owns (E_{v.2}) and leaves along the twin's edge, uses positive scalar multiples (orientation), identifies {i,j} = v.1.val with i ≠ j, and records ρ_S(v) = ρ(visitTwin v) and the ownership of the predecessor and successor marks.

`unselected_visit_straight` (124-135) and `smoothing_corner_transverse` (137-138) hold for every unselected/selected visit with no ownership hypothesis (they are properties of the marked circle and of P), which is more than the per-carrier statement the source makes.

`traced_marks`/`traced_successor`/`traced_sides` (102-120) give explicit list-level certificates (Nodup, positive length, per-side continuity, cyclic gluing, ρ_S-successor formula with `%`) that the printed prose only implies.
`neighbor_visits` (147-148) is phrased for every visit v of x (v vs. visitTwin v), i.e. symmetric in the two visits.
weaker_than_source: Representation note, not a missing clause: the 'closed polygonal curve in ℝ²' is not one object (a subset of the plane or a continuous closed map); it is the cyclic list of plane points `componentPlaneCycle` (CarrierClosedTrace 66-69, whose own docstring says 'not yet a continuous circle map') together with the per-side maps `componentTraceEdge` and the gluing/continuity facts of `traced_sides`. These finite data determine the curve, so nothing printed is lost.

Representation note: `componentCornerCycle` is a `Cycle (Mark P)`, whereas the printed corners are points of the plane. That distinct corner marks of one carrier are distinct plane points (a carrier never owns both visits of a selected crossing) is not in this bundle; it follows from `distinct_carriers` in the accepted conv:selected-visits row (SelectedVisitsConvention 55-56) and generic injectivity of crossing points.

Representation note: 'partitions Γ(P) into closed cycles' is rendered on the marks (cycles of ρ_S) with the arcs between marks carried implicitly as the straight sides; the point set Γ(P) itself is not partitioned in Lean. This is the finite successor model that the brief accepts as context (sm-3 96-116).

No clause states directly that deleting the unselected-visit points from `componentPlaneCycle` leaves the traced curve unchanged (or that the traced curve equals the polygon on the evaluated `componentCornerCycle`); this is implied by `unselected_visit_straight` (collinear, same-direction incoming and outgoing pieces) but is not spelled out as an equality of curves.

adversarial_refutations.argument: After expanding every local definition in work/reviews/def-smoothing-reviewer-input-statement.lean.txt to accepted primitives, I found no place where the Lean statement is weaker than sm-3-statesum.tex:14-27, adds a hypothesis, quantifies differently, or uses a local definition that fails to denote the printed object. Specifically for the three targeted encodings: (1) componentPlaneCycle (CarrierClosedTrace.lean:66-69) is `map eval (componentMarkList q)` where componentMarkList = markList.filter (owner = q) is the owned marks in inherited traversal order (markList = Finset.univ.sort by traversalKey (i,t) = i.val + t, the cyclic order of def:gauss); traced_marks (nodup, exactly the owned marks) plus traced_successor `ρ_S (L[i]) = L[(i+1) % len]` force L to list the ρ_S-orbit in ρ_S order, so no mark-ordering mismatch is possible. (2) componentTraceEdge (CarrierClosedTrace.lean:104-112) uses index `(i.val+1) % L.length`, so the side from L[len-1] back to L[0] is present; traced_sides certifies each side equals smoothingSegment(L[i]) (segment from eval(L[i]) to eval(ρ_S L[i])), has positive length, glues (edge i at 1 = edge (i+1)%len at 0) and is continuous. Because eval(a) = eval(visitTwin a) and ρ_S(a) = ρ(visitTwin a), smoothingSegment a at a selected visit is exactly the outgoing arc at the twin, so the traced curve is the union of the printed reconnected arcs. (3) IsTrueCorner (CarrierTrueCorners.lean:44-46) marks vertices and selected visits; componentCornerCycle filters componentCycle by it. Under G1 (no three vertices collinear) a vertex lies on no edge except E_{i-1}, E_i, and under G2 (no triple point) a crossing point lies only on its two edges, while every side is a sub-segment of one edge between consecutive marks; hence a carrier's curve passes through μ_i or x_{ij} only via a mark it owns, so owned vertex/selected-visit marks are exactly the printed corners. unselected_visit_straight gives straight passage (incoming on E_{v.2}, both directions positive multiples of ℓ̃_{v.2}) at unselected visits, so those points are not corners and keeping them in the Cycle Plane does not change the traced curve; smoothing_corner gives arrival along ℓ̃_{v.2} and departure along ℓ̃_{(visitTwin v).2} with the crossing identified as {v.2, twin.2}, and smoothing_corner_transverse gives det ≠ 0, i.e. a genuine turn. The source requires a turn only at S-crossings, not at vertices, so no vertex clause is missing. Reconnection is ρ_S = ρ ∘ selectedMarkPerm S with selectedMarkPerm an involution swapping the two visits of each selected crossing, giving ρ_S(a)=ρ(b) and ρ_S(b)=ρ(a) ("for both visits"). crossings_of / crossing_count match "x ∈ X(P)∖S both of whose visits lie on Q" (visits of x are exactly the v with v.1 = x; ownership equals geometric incidence by the G1/G2 argument) and m_Q. supportNeighbors = {y | ∃ x ∈ S, Interlaces y x} = N(S) of def:interlace; neighbor_visits / neighbor_no_carrier match the last sentence. Domain is ∀ k ≥ 3, ∀ generic P, ∀ decomposition S (IsDecomposition = S ∈ independentSupports, accepted); `∀ _ : NeZero k` is a subsingleton implied by 3 ≤ k. The only differences are strengthenings: vertex_corner (arrival along ℓ̃_{i-1}, departure along ℓ̃_i), the specific edge assignment in smoothing_corner, smoothing_corner_transverse, and unselected_visit_straight quantified over all unselected visits without an owner hypothesis.
